data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense fails on Popper's own terms because it conflates 'preference for action' with 'rational expectation of success.' Popper explicitly rejected the idea that past survival (fitness) provides any logical basis for expecting future performance; to prefer a theory *because* it is fit implies an inductive bet that the environment will remain stable enough for that fitness to matter. The evolutionary analogy describes how theories survive, not why a scientist is rational to *choose* one for practical application without assuming the future resembles the past. By framing preference as 'natural selection,' the target smuggles in the very inductive assumption (that the fittest today will work tomorrow) that Popper sought to eliminate, rendering the preference indefensible strictly within his anti-inductive framework.
